title: Neuschwanstein Castle
blurb: King Ludwig II of Bavaria’s Romanesque Revival palace above the Pöllat Gorge, built from 1869 as an inhabitable stage set for Wagner’s operas. At 65 m it is the tallest castle in the world, while its planned 90 m keep was never built.

sourceUrls.label: German Federal Foreign Office: UNESCO inscription 2025
TravelPulse: Bavaria’s palaces added to UNESCO list
History Tools: The Fantastical History of Neuschwanstein Castle

systems.name: Gatehouse
systems.description: The symmetrical entrance block flanked by two stair towers, with red brick outer walls, yellow limestone court fronts, a crow-stepped gable and the king’s first lodging.

systems.name: Lower courtyard
systems.description: The lower court level with the gallery building, the Rectangular Tower foundations and the embankment marking the choir of the projected chapel.

systems.name: Palas
systems.description: The colossal five-storey main building: two huge cuboids joined at a flat angle under two adjacent high gable roofs, with frescoes, balconies and turrets.

systems.name: Towers
systems.description: The 65 m north stair tower, the tallest castle tower in the world, the south stair tower, the 45 m Rectangular Tower and the Palas corner turrets.

systems.name: Upper courtyard
systems.description: The upper court level with the Knights’ House, the Bower, the blind arcade gallery and the foundations of the unbuilt 90 m keep.

systems.name: Roofs and chimneys
systems.description: Gable roof slabs and the numerous decorative chimneys spangling the roofs.

systems.name: Throne Hall
systems.description: The 20 by 12 m hall in the west wing, 13 m high across two floors, with arcades on three sides and an apse for the never-completed throne.

systems.name: Hall of the Singers
systems.description: The 27 by 10 m hall in the east wing, the largest room of the palace, with its gallery, tribune and the arcaded Sängerlaube stage.

systems.name: King’s rooms
systems.description: The third-floor lodging: drawing room, artificial grotto, study, dining room, bedroom and house chapel, with the kitchen and servants’ rooms below.

systems.name: Rock terrace and gorge
systems.description: The cliff-ridge terrace carrying the 150 m ensemble, the gorge of the Pöllat stream and the steel Marienbrücke.
